conflicts.meeting_title: DPS Board of Education — May 22, 2014 Regular Monthly Meeting
conflicts.issue: Inclusion and Voting Role of Newly Elected Board Members in Superintendent Search Interviews
conflicts.summary: The seated Board split 5-2 on adding the issue to the agenda and 4-3 on final passage over whether newly elected Board members (taking office July 1) should participate in Superintendent Search candidate interviews in an advisory role, be excluded altogether, or be granted voting privileges.
conflicts.side_a_position: Include newly elected Board members under confidentiality agreements to review applications, attend interviews, and provide advisory input while leaving the final hiring vote to the seated Board.
side_a_arguments: Including incoming Board members gathers valuable insight from those who will work with the new Superintendent and builds a collaborative governance team.
State statute permits only an advisory role until newly elected members are sworn in on July 1, as confirmed by Board Attorney Ken Soo.
conflicts.side_b_position: Either exclude newly elected Board members from the outgoing Board's interview process or require that they be given full voting privileges (with Omega Curtis Parker also asking if seated members could rotate off early).
side_b_arguments: Fredrick A. Davis moved to reject Chair Carter's proposal and warned he would not participate in the interviews if newly elected members took part under those terms.
If newly elected members were included, Davis and Forte-Brown moved a substitute to grant them full voting privileges rather than non-voting participation.
conflicts.resolution: After defeating exclusion (3-4), a non-binding vote amendment (1-6, supported only by Nancy Cox), and voting privileges (3-4), the Board passed Natalie Beyer's motion 4-3 to include newly elected members in a confidential advisory capacity; Omega Curtis Parker voted with the majority on adding the item (5-2) but aligned with Minnie Forte-Brown and Fredrick A. Davis on all four substantive votes.

meetings.title: DPS Board of Education — May 22, 2014 Regular Monthly Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 22, 2014 Regular Monthly Meeting with all seven members present, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education experienced a sharp, multi-vote split over including newly elected Board members in the Superintendent Search interview process. The Board voted 5-2 twice—Ayes: Heidi Carter, Natalie Beyer, Leigh Bordley, Nancy Cox, and Omega Curtis Parker; Nays: Minnie Forte-Brown and Fredrick A. Davis—to add the item and approve the amended agenda, then defeated a motion by Fredrick A. Davis to reject inclusion 3-4 (Ayes: Minnie Forte-Brown, Fredrick A. Davis, and Omega Curtis Parker; Nays: Heidi Carter, Natalie Beyer, Nancy Cox, and Leigh Bordley). After Board Attorney Ken Soo advised that newly elected members could not legally cast binding votes before July 1, an amendment for a non-binding vote failed 1-6 (Aye: Nancy Cox; Nays: Heidi Carter, Minnie Forte-Brown, Fredrick A. Davis, Omega Curtis Parker, Leigh Bordley, and Natalie Beyer), a substitute motion granting full voting privileges failed 3-4 (Ayes: Minnie Forte-Brown, Fredrick A. Davis, and Omega Curtis Parker; Nays: Heidi Carter, Nancy Cox, Leigh Bordley, and Natalie Beyer), and the main motion allowing newly elected members to review applications, attend interviews, and debrief confidentially in an advisory role passed 4-3 (Ayes: Heidi Carter, Natalie Beyer, Leigh Bordley, and Nancy Cox; Nays: Minnie Forte-Brown, Fredrick A. Davis, and Omega Curtis Parker). The Board unanimously approved prior minutes (7-0), the Consent Agenda including Eno Valley HVAC and Y.E. Smith kitchen hood projects (7-0), Revised Magnet Policy 4131 (7-0), district-wide expansion of the Universal Free Breakfast Program for 2014-2015 (7-0), and May 22 Personnel Reports (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Heidi Carter called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. and led a moment of silence. The Board recognized May Student of the Month Xavier Smith, Get Involved Award recipient Steve Rigsbee, EC awardees Deanna St. John and Denise Nelson, state Quill writing champions at Lucas Middle, Science competition teams (Team 900, Githens Gravity Games, Envirothon, Jordan Rocketry), and community partners; Interim Superintendent Hugh Osteen celebrated Early College/CMA/Middle College graduations, held a moment of silence for late student Aaron Bagley, and Vice Chair Minnie Forte-Brown presented the D-WORK youth employment initiative.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval (Addition of Superintendent Search Participation)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Carter requested adding consideration of including newly elected Board members in the Superintendent Search interview process. Nancy Cox moved and Natalie Beyer seconded adding the item, passing 5-2, and the amended agenda passed 5-2 with Minnie Forte-Brown and Fredrick A. Davis opposed on both votes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three speakers addressed the Board (Minnie Harrington was absent): Denise Johnson read a letter regarding a school bullying incident; Minister Paul Scott criticized funding the G.R.E.A.T. program and recommended two books on race and criminalization; and DEA President Andrea Underwood called eliminating teacher career status unconstitutional, thanked the Board for joining Guilford County in the 25% contract lawsuit, and praised Office of Student Assignment staff.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Minutes and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved four sets of April–May 2014 meeting minutes (7-0) and a six-item Consent Agenda covering increased attorney fees, Eno Valley Elementary HVAC installation bids and equipment purchase order, 2014-2015 E-Rate applications, construction management services extension, and Y.E. Smith Elementary kitchen hood replacement bids (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Inclusion of Newly Elected Board Members in Superintendent Search Interview Process
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members debated Chair Carter's proposal to let newly elected members sign confidentiality agreements, review applications, attend candidate interviews, and debrief in an advisory capacity while the seated Board made the final hiring vote. After defeating a motion to reject inclusion (3-4), an amendment for a non-binding vote (1-6), and a substitute motion to grant voting privileges (3-4) following legal advice from Attorney Ken Soo, the Board passed the advisory-role motion 4-3; Pastor Fredrick Davis stated he would not participate in the interviews and confirmed with Attorney Soo that doing so carried no criminal liability.

agenda_items.title: Support Services Committee: Revised Policy 4131 — Programs Magnet Schools (Second Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Omega Curtis Parker and Dr. Debbie Pitman presented second-reading revisions to Policy 4131 addressing late assignment priorities to Josephine Dobbs Early College for students transferring from other Early College programs and Policy 4131.2.H.

agenda_items.title: Administrative Services Committee: Child Nutrition Services — Universal Free Breakfast
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Assistant Superintendent Scott Denton and Child Nutrition Director James Keaton reported that a 22-school Universal Free Breakfast pilot generated reimbursement gains exceeding lost meal revenue while reducing stigma and negative meal balances. The Board unanimously approved expanding 'Breakfast Is On Us!' to all DPS schools in 2014-2015.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Open Session Personnel Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board entered closed session at 9:04 p.m. for student, personnel, and attorney-client matters, reconvened in open session at 10:41 p.m., unanimously approved the May 22, 2014 Personnel Reports, and adjourned at 10:42 p.m.

meetings.title: BOE May 12, 2014
meetings.executive_summary: At a special budget adoption meeting on May 12, 2014, Chair Heidi Carter presided over final consideration of the district's FY 2014-2015 budget request to Durham County and a FY 2013-2014 one-time funding proposal. Following presentations by Interim Superintendent Hugh Osteen and Chief Finance Officer Aaron Beaulieu comparing two $407,932,921 budget options, the Board unanimously approved Option 2 by voice vote (7-0)—requesting $120,949,141 in total County funding (including an extra $716,000 to offset charter-school growth and halve reliance on committed fund balance), planning for a 2% staff raise if state-funded, and prioritizing an additional interpreter position and district-wide bilingual/social-worker family support services. The Board also unanimously approved the FY 2013-2014 one-time funding proposal (7-0) using lapsed salaries and current funds for $500 supplements to licensed instructional staff, $250 supplements to classified staff (excluding ELT and the Superintendent), Read to Achieve needs, and $725,000 for facility maintenance before adjourning.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Heidi Carter called the special meeting to order (inadvertently saying May 13) to complete final budget approval for submission to Durham County by May 15, led a moment of silence, and called for approval of Item 3 (the agenda), which passed unanimously by voice vote at 00:05:11.

agenda_items.title: Adoption of Proposed FY 2014-2015 Budget Request (Option 2)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Hugh Osteen and CFO Aaron Beaulieu presented two versions of the $407,932,921 proposed 2014-15 budget breaking out $15,660,210 in charter school pass-throughs, full quarter-cent sales tax funding, and $1,370,000 in capital outlay. Board members clarified that Option 2's footnoted priorities covered district-wide bilingual family support and social-worker needs, reduced fund-balance dependency by roughly 50% via an added $716,000 County request (to $120,949,141 total), and planned for a 2% staff raise if funded by the state; the Board unanimously approved Option 2 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Approval of FY 2013-2014 One-Time Money Proposal
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff clarified that the one-time funding proposal used lapsed salaries and current-year dollars to provide $500 payments to licensed instructional personnel and $250 to all classified employees (excluding Executive Leadership Team and the Superintendent), along with Read to Achieve funding and $725,000 to restore facility maintenance operations after prior cuts. After Chair Carter clarified the motion applied to the 2013-2014 school year, the Board unanimously approved the proposal by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: County Submission Timeline and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim Superintendent Osteen confirmed the approved budget request would be transmitted to Durham County before Thursday, May 15, and noted ongoing coordination with County Manager Davis on presentation scheduling before the meeting adjourned at 00:26:52.

agenda_items.title: Approval of Board of Education Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following discussion of six sets of June–August 2013 minutes, Leigh Bordley flagged wording issues regarding speaker Eddie Davis and two omitted board member names on page 5 of the June 27 minutes, and Fredrick A. Davis withdrew his earlier motion. Bordley then moved to approve the minutes with the understanding that Ms. Gates would review the recording and make those corrections, seconded by Natalie Beyer.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board approved eight consent items covering Y.E. Smith Elementary emergency summer repairs, Neal Middle mobile classroom bids, Easley Elementary asphalt paving bids, criminal background check bids, the Driver's Education salary schedule, the Museum of Life and Science partnership, and contracts with Discovery Education and Signature Learning Resources, Inc. Nancy Cox moved approval, seconded by Omega Curtis Parker.

agenda_items.title: Reports of the Board: Advocacy Liaisons, Modified Meeting Schedule, and NCSBAC
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously reappointed Natalie Beyer as Federal Liaison and Nancy Cox as State Liaison (7-0) on a motion by Minnie Forte-Brown seconded by Leigh Bordley. On Chair Heidi Carter's proposal to move Closed Session to 4:30 p.m. prior to the Open Meeting, Fredrick A. Davis opposed the change, so no schedule modification was adopted; on the $8,000 NC School Boards Action Center (NCSBAC) request presented by Forte-Brown, the Board agreed by unanimous consent to defer further discussion and a vote to a future meeting (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Administrative Services Committee: Resolution Opposing the State Education Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Natalie Beyer outlined the 2013-15 NC General Assembly budget's impact—citing $2.8 billion in tax cuts, elimination of teacher assistants and master's pay incentives, a $10 million voucher program, teacher salary freezes, and local DPS cuts of 113.5 teachers, 85 teacher assistants, and 6 instructional support positions totaling $4.2 million beyond worst projections. Board members took turns reading the resolution opposing the treatment of North Carolina's children and educators, which passed unanimously on a motion by Fredrick A. Davis seconded by Leigh Bordley.

agenda_items.title: Instructional Services Committee: Measurement Incorporated Contract for NC Write
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Committee Chair Leigh Bordley introduced Dr. Lewis Ferebee and Dr. Teresa Daye to present the 2013-16 NC Write contract serving roughly 27,456 students in grades 2-12, which passed unanimously on a motion by Fredrick A. Davis seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown. Dr. Ferebee confirmed in response to Natalie Beyer that teacher participation is optional and that the Chewning reference raised during public comment reflected prior-year enrollment data.

agenda_items.title: Support Services Committee: Durham County DSS Contract, Revised Policy 4132.7, and Family Academy
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Board unanimously approved the annual Durham County Department of Social Services professional services contract (strengthening DPS input on interviews, principals' roles, and performance feedback) on a motion by Omega Curtis Parker seconded by Fredrick A. Davis (7-0). The Board also unanimously approved Revised Policy 4132.7 on second reading allowing calendar-magnet school teachers (excluding Central Services staff) to request transfers for their children to another calendar magnet when their child's grade is unavailable at their workplace (7-0), and heard an informational update from Kendra O'Neal-Williams and Dietrich Danner on the DPS Family Academy.
